label: lr-9475d
summary: The model adds a linear score in most inputs to three nonlinear parts. Sodium has a U-shaped effect: for a typical patient the predicted risk is lowest at 138 mmol/L (6%) and rises steeply below 134 mmol/L (a hyponatraemia hinge acting through a renal unit) and above 140 mmol/L (hypernatraemia hinges), and switching the sodium part off moves the training AUC from 0.904 to 0.752. Systolic pressure and heart rate interact with opposite slopes: the risk rises with pressure at a slow pulse and falls with it at a fast pulse, so discordant pairs score high (mean predicted risk 84.3% for the 63 training patients with high pressure and a slow pulse, 77.8% for the 52 with low pressure and a fast pulse) and concordant pairs low. Age, creatinine and smoking raise the risk, and so, mostly, does diabetes; a gate that opens with age and leanness in non-diabetic men (open for 0 women or diabetic patients) adds risk through the renal unit, so for an older, lean man diabetes lowers the predicted risk (28% without, 15% with); the noise column has a small fitted effect.

resisted: The readings of the gate chain are approximate. sex_diabetes_gate reads as older non-diabetic men (probe score 0.89), but BMI and the high-sodium unit also move it, which that concept leaves out. renal_228 reads as low sodium or being a non-diabetic man (score 0.81), a sum that ignores how age and BMI set the gate's size. The direct part is a linear sum, described by its formula, not by one concept (score 0.47, closed form only). bp_hr is a large leaf of eight units read as one interaction; its exits are read by different concepts, and where the crossover sits depends on BMI, the renal unit and the old-and-lean hinge. The model's use of the noise column (through a sodium unit and a direct edge) has no domain reading: it looks fitted.

leaves.name: low_sodium
leaves.why: A hyponatraemia hinge: on exactly for sodium at or below the threshold and growing linearly as sodium falls.

leaves.name: high_sodium
leaves.why: Hypernatraemia hinges rising linearly above the upper threshold; the second unit also reads the noise column.

leaves.name: age_bmi
leaves.why: An older-and-leaner hinge passed on as a near copy and a higher-threshold copy that feed the gate and the blood-pressure part.

leaves.name: sex_diabetes_gate
leaves.why: A gate open only for non-diabetic men, widening with age and leanness and closed by high sodium.

leaves.name: renal_228
leaves.why: An alarm unit that fires for low sodium or an open sex-diabetes gate, raised further by creatinine and smoking.

leaves.name: bp_hr
leaves.why: A systolic pressure by heart rate interaction with opposite slopes: discordant pressure and pulse give high risk, concordant low.

leaves.name: direct
leaves.why: The linear sum of the direct input edges, described by its formula rather than by one concept.

overall_function: The network adds a linear score over most inputs to three nonlinear parts. Sodium has a U-shaped effect with hinges at the low and the high end of the normal range, the low arm acting through an alarm unit that also responds to creatinine and smoking. Systolic pressure and heart rate interact with opposite slopes, so the score is high when one is high and the other low and low when both move together. Age, BMI and creatinine act mostly as rising terms; a gate for older, lean, non-diabetic men adds risk through the alarm unit, so for those patients diabetes and female sex lower the score; male sex has no direct term, and the noise column has a small fitted effect through a sodium unit and a direct edge.
clinical_terms: The model flags both hyponatraemia and hypernatraemia: the predicted risk is lowest in the middle of the normal sodium range and climbs steeply below its low end and above its high end. It scores haemodynamic discordance as dangerous: a high systolic pressure with a slow pulse, or a low pressure with a fast pulse (a shock-index-like pattern), carries a high predicted risk, while high pressure with a fast pulse, or low pressure with a slow pulse, carries a low one. Older age, higher creatinine and smoking raise the risk throughout, and an older, lean man without diabetes gets an extra rise through the same alarm unit that hyponatraemia uses. The dependence on the noise column has no clinical reading and looks fitted.
stuck: Little stopped the work. The entangled topology needed eight identity nodes on cross-leaf hidden edges plus ten input splits before any leaf could be annotated. query_linearise at parts level failed (tool bug, nodes level used). Splitting the first metabolic-gate leaf after its partial probe grade meant re-running every query and remapping every placeholder.
